messages.subject: Wait for a resource to be free
parts:
Hello!

I don't quiet understand how queue_size, capacity_size, and wait() work together. 
Pls, share a simmer code of the following  toy system with 1 queue and 2 servers(resources ):
1) Users arrive to a limited queue (say queue_size = 10).
2) In order to be served,  an user must wait in the queue till one of the two available resources is free.
3) Once an user is server, it leaves the system.

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Wait for a resource to be free
parts:
On Wed, 24 Feb 2021 at 23:19, N!P <cuys...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello!
>
> I don't quiet understand how queue_size, capacity_size, and wait() work together.

Because they do not work together, these are independent
functionalities. Resources have their capacity and queue sizes, which
imply how many arrivals can be served at the same time, and how many
arrivals can stay waiting to be served without being rejected. On the
other hand, wait() is a function that an arrival can use to pause
until a signal is received, and has nothing to do with resources.

> Pls, share a simmer code of the following toy system with 1 queue and 2 servers(resources ):
> 1) Users arrive to a limited queue (say queue_size = 10).
> 2) In order to be served, an user must wait in the queue till one of the two available resources is free.
> 3) Once an user is server, it leaves the system.

There are numerous examples in the documentation, including systems
with limited capacity as well as examples with asynchronous events
that use trap/wait/send.
